transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thanks for seeing me. Um, I guess I'm here because... well, I feel like I'm always running a bit hot, you know? Like I just can't shut the motor off. I mean, usually it's a good thing, especially in my line of work as a firefighter, being ready to go and all. But, um, lately, it's been getting me into a little bit of trouble at the firehouse. Nothing too crazy, I hope, but... I just wanted to make sure everything's okay. Is that... does that make sense?
During these times when your motor feels like it's running, do you find you need much less sleep than usual while still feeling full of energy?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I definitely need my sleep. It's not like I'm staying up all night or doing anything... weird like that. I get pretty wiped out just like anyone else, especially after a long shift at the station. 

So, no, I don't think I need less sleep at all. I try to be really good about getting my rest, actually. I hope that's normal? Like, the motor running thing is just a daytime energy thing, mostly. Did I answer that okay?
Do you find yourself constantly worrying about many different things, and having a hard time controlling those worries?

No, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier. I mean, everyone gets a little stressed sometimes, right? But I don't sit around dwelling on things or letting my mind spin out of control with bad thoughts. I try to just focus on what's in front of me and handle it. I hope that's the right way to handle things? I just... I don't feel like I'm an anxious person or anything like that. Is that what you were asking?
Has this feeling of your motor constantly running been present since you were a child?

Um, yeah, actually... I guess it has. My mom says I was pretty much exactly like this back in grade school, too. I mean, I was just a really energetic kid, you know? Always popping out of my seat, or, um, blurting out answers a little too quickly. Just eager to participate, mostly! 

But... well, I did end up losing my homework a lot, and... I guess I got my fair share of notes sent home from the teachers. Which I always felt terrible about, I really didn't want to cause trouble or be a burden. They always told my mom I was bright enough to do the work, I just... had a hard time channeling all that energy. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid? I really did try my best to be good. Is that... does that sound like normal kid stuff to you?

latest_inference.note: Childhood onset of hyperactivity, impulsivity, and inattention confirms ADHD, ruling out F43.1.
